newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG seeks to block CalEnergy shr purchase.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG seeks to block CalEnergy shr purchase.

text.p: Hostile takeover target New York State Electric & Gas Corp said Wednesday it has asked the New York State Public Service Commission to prohibit bidder CalEnergy Co Inc from acquiring any shares of the firm without regulatory approval.

In a statement released by the Binghamton, N.Y.-based utility, NYSEG also challenged CalEnergy's acquisition effort, contending the Nebraska-based independent power producer does not have the experience to run the company.
"To date, there has been no demonstration of CalEnergy's fitness to run NYSEG...It has no experience in the difficult distribution of natural gas," NYSEG said.

In seeking the ruling from state regulators, NYSEG cited Section 70 of the New York Public Service Law, which it said requires companies to receive commission approval before acquiring securities of a gas or electric company.
CalEnergy has launched a $24.50 per share tender offer for 9.9 percent of NYSEG shares as the first step in an effort to buy the whole company in a transaction valued at $1.9 billion.
CalEnergy quickly challenged NYSEG's demand, saying the state law only applies to electric utilities.

"This is utter nonsense. CalEnergy is not an electric utility in the state of New York and does not charge ratepayers for the supply and distribution of electricity as NYSEG well knows. This is another desperate act by a very entrenched management," a company spokeswoman said.
